messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Adjusting Bins in geom_histogram
parts:
Dear All,
Please consider the code snippet at the end of the email.
I generate random lognormal deviates, then round them up to integers and
remove the values equal to zero and create a histogram (on a semilog
scale) with the remaining numbers.
By construction, there are no numbers smaller than 1 left.
However, when I run the script on my machine, I see that the generated
bin structure creates a first bin (probably) given by (10^-0.3, 10^0].
Technically speaking there is nothing wrong with it, but if I look at it
I get the impression that the distribution actually contains values
smaller than one.
My first question is then
(1)How can I change this? In other words, can I fine tune
geom_histogram() without using layer() and stat_bin? I would like my
first bin to be like [10^0, 10^0.3).

My second question is the following
(2) If I add a zero value to the random deviates, i.e.
contact <- c(0,round(rlnorm(10000,1,1.2))) after setting the seed and
remove the line that forces contact to contains only integers >=1, then
I would expect ggplot2 to complain (it cannot place a zero on the log
scale on the x axis), whereas the generated histogram pretty much stays
the same.
Am I misunderstanding something pretty basic?

(3) How can I get a list of the breaks used to generate the histogram?

Many thanks

Lorenzo

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1234)
contact <- round(rlnorm(10000,1,1.2))
contact <- contact[which(contact>0)]
contact <- as.data.frame(contact)
names(contact) <- "contact_data"

gpl <- ggplot(contact,aes(x=contact_data,y=..count../sum(..count..)))+
geom_histogram(binwidth=.2, colour="darkgreen", fill="white")+
scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10")+
xlab("Contact Duration (sec)")+
ylab("Pairwise Number of Contacts")+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))


pdf("final_bin_plot.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

Use the breaks argument to specify exactly where the breaks occur.

> My second question is the following
> (2) If I add a zero value to the random deviates, i.e.
> contact <- c(0,round(rlnorm(10000,1,1.2))) after setting the seed and remove
> the line that forces contact to contains only integers >=1, then I would
> expect ggplot2 to complain (it cannot place a zero on the log scale on the x
> axis), whereas the generated histogram pretty much stays the same.
> Am I misunderstanding something pretty basic?

A simpler reproducible example is this:

df <- data.frame(x = 0:2)
ggplot(df, aes(x)) + geom_bar(binwidth = 1, colour = "black")
ggplot(df, aes(x)) + geom_bar(binwidth = 1, colour = "black") + scale_x_log10()

and it seems like missing values are being silently dropped. I'll add
it to the to do list -
http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/#issue/68
> (3) How can I get a list of the breaks used to generate the histogram?

Unfortunately there isn't currently any easy way, except to inspect
the source code of the bins function. I should extract that logic out
into its own function -
http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/#issue/67

Hadley
